body:
The HiCache storage key carries the model name and the TP/PP/CP geometry, but not the KV cache dtype. In `HiCacheFile`, `config_suffix` is built from `model_name`, `tp_rank/tp_size` (non-MLA), `pp_size/pp_rank`, and the CP slice (`hicache_storage.py:378-386`) — nothing dtype-related. The root cause sits one level up: `HiCacheStorageConfig` itself has no dtype field, so no backend can include it.

Consequence: two server runs on the same model with different `--kv-cache-dtype` (e.g. bf16, then fp8_e4m3) produce identical keys, and the second run silently reuses cache entries whose bytes are in the wrong format.

I have a fix for the core key derivation, but a complete fix has to cover every backend's key path — hf3fs keys off a file-path prefix, and flexkv/lmcache/aibrix derive keys inside external client libraries — so I'm filing this first to agree on the approach before a PR. Partial coverage on a silent-corruption bug seems worse than none. My suggestion: add the dtype to `HiCacheStorageConfig` and thread it into each backend's key derivation, with backends that cannot guarantee it refusing loudly rather than colliding silently.
title: [Bug] HiCache storage keys omit kv_cache_dtype — silent cross-run cache collisions
